beats.vo: Hey champ, welcome back! Pixi and I are so glad you're here.
beats.caption: Welcome back, champ!

beats.vo: Last time, we learned that AI is maths, not magic. It finds patterns in lots of examples, and then it makes a guess. And sometimes, that guess is wrong!
beats.caption: Last time: AI finds patterns, then guesses

beats.vo: Today is chapter two of, What Is AI? It's called, Smart versus Simple.
beats.caption: Chapter 2 · Smart vs. Simple

beats.vo: Here's a puzzle for you. Is every gadget with a button, AI? Hmm. Let's find out.
beats.caption: Is every gadget with a button AI?

beats.vo: It's Saturday morning at Kabir's house. Ring, ring, ring! His alarm clock goes off at six thirty. Ugh. It's a holiday!
beats.caption: 6:30 on a Saturday. Ring, ring!

beats.vo: Later, the power goes out. His little sister Mini grabs a torch, clicks it on, and shouts, wow! This torch is so smart. It must be AI!
beats.caption: Mini: "This torch is so smart. It's AI!"

beats.vo: Is Mini right? Is a torch AI? What do you think?
beats.caption: Is a torch AI? What do you think?

beats.vo: Let's find out. Because there are two kinds of programs. Simple ones, and smart ones. By the end of today, you'll tell them apart like a detective!
beats.caption: Two kinds: simple and smart

beats.vo: Simple programs follow fixed rules. A fixed rule is an instruction that never changes.
beats.caption: Simple programs follow FIXED RULES

beats.vo: Like a doorbell. If the button is pressed, play a sound. Press it today. Ding dong! Press it next week. Ding dong! Exactly the same.
beats.caption: If the button is pressed → play a sound

beats.vo: Kabir's alarm clock has a fixed rule too. At six thirty, ring. Monday, ring. Saturday, ring. Even on his birthday, ring!
beats.caption: At 6:30 → ring. Every single day!

beats.vo: And Mini's torch? Switch on, light on. Switch off, light off. That's it. One fixed rule.
beats.caption: Torch: switch on → light on

beats.vo: Here's the key thing. A simple program never learns anything new. The alarm clock will never figure out that Kabir likes to sleep in on Saturdays.
beats.caption: Simple programs never learn anything new

beats.vo: Quick question. Tomorrow is Sunday, and Kabir really wants to sleep late. What will his alarm clock do at six thirty? Think!
beats.caption: Sunday, 6:30. What will the alarm do?

beats.vo: Ring, ring, ring! Of course. It follows its fixed rule, no matter what. It can't learn that Sunday is different. Poor Kabir!
beats.caption: Ring! The fixed rule never changes.

beats.vo: Now, smart programs, like AI, are different. They learn from examples. And they change what they do, after seeing more examples.
beats.caption: AI learns from examples, and changes

beats.vo: Learning here doesn't mean thinking like you do. It just means the program gets better at its job, by looking at more and more examples.
beats.caption: Learning = getting better from more examples

beats.vo: Think of a voice assistant. At first, it might mix up your words. But it hears millions of voices. Voices from Delhi, Chennai, Kolkata, and everywhere!
beats.caption: A voice assistant hears millions of voices

beats.vo: Over time, it gets better at understanding all kinds of accents. More examples, better guesses!
beats.caption: More examples → better at understanding

beats.vo: Here's another one. Spellcheck. You're typing a message to your nani. You want to type, because, but oops, the letters get mixed up.
beats.caption: Oops! You type "becuase"

beats.vo: And spellcheck suggests, because! How does it know? It learned common words from lots and lots of writing.
beats.caption: Spellcheck learned words from lots of writing

beats.vo: Or photo search. Type dog in a photo app, and it finds all your dog pictures. It learned what dogs look like, from lots of example photos.
beats.caption: Photo search learned from example photos

beats.vo: And remember Kabir's cricket cartoons? Video suggestions change too, as you watch more. Watch lots of animal videos, and soon, you'll see more animals!
beats.caption: Video suggestions change as you watch more

beats.vo: So here's a super question, to test any gadget. Does it change what it does, after more examples?
beats.caption: Does it change after more examples?

beats.vo: If yes, it may be AI. Like the voice assistant, or spellcheck. They keep getting better with more examples.
beats.caption: Yes → it may be AI

beats.vo: If no, it's a simple, fixed rule program. Like the doorbell. Does it have a screen? Is it expensive? Those questions don't help. Only this one does!
beats.caption: No → a simple, fixed-rule program

beats.vo: Let's play, sort it! Fixed rule, or learns from examples?
beats.caption: Sort it: fixed rule, or learns?

beats.vo: Alarm clock. Spellcheck. Doorbell. Voice assistant. Calculator. Photo search. Which ones learn from examples? Pause, and think.
beats.caption: Which ones learn from examples?

beats.vo: The alarm clock, doorbell, and calculator follow fixed rules. Spellcheck, the voice assistant, and photo search learn from examples. How did you do? Oh, and a ceiling fan switch? Fixed rule too!
beats.caption: 3 follow fixed rules · 3 learn from examples

beats.vo: Now, one more big idea. Who makes all these programs? People! The person who writes and plans a program is called a designer.
beats.caption: A DESIGNER writes and plans a program

beats.vo: People design the doorbell's simple rule. If pressed, play a sound. And people design AI too. They write the program, and they test it.
beats.caption: People design simple programs AND AI

beats.vo: People even choose the examples that AI learns from. Like picking thousands of cat photos, to teach it what a cat looks like.
beats.caption: People choose the examples AI learns from

beats.vo: So AI doesn't build itself out of nothing. Every AI has human designers. People are still in charge.
beats.caption: AI doesn't build itself. People are in charge!

beats.vo: Okay champ, it's practice check time, just like the quiz.
beats.caption: Your turn: practice check

beats.vo: Remember Mini? Is a torch AI? Why, or why not? Pause the video, and think. Or write your answer on paper.
beats.caption: Is a torch AI? Why or why not?

beats.vo: No, it's not! A torch follows one fixed rule. Switch on, light on. It never learns from examples, and it never changes what it does. Sorry, Mini! Great thinking, champ.
beats.caption: No! One fixed rule. It never learns or changes.

beats.vo: Let's remember. Simple programs follow fixed rules, like a doorbell.
beats.caption: Simple programs follow fixed rules

beats.vo: AI changes what it does, after seeing more examples.
beats.caption: AI changes after seeing more examples

beats.vo: A torch is not AI. It just follows a switch.
beats.caption: A torch is not AI. It just follows a switch.

beats.vo: And people design both simple programs, and AI.
beats.caption: People design both

beats.vo: Chapter two, done! Now you can tell smart from simple, champ.
beats.caption: Chapter 2 done!

beats.vo: Now let's see what you remember. Tap Finish, and try the quiz. You've got this!
beats.caption: Next: Quiz · Tap Finish
